jobs.description:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Governance team helps shape how the company responsibly develops and deploys increasingly capable AI. We bring together technical evidence, policy, and operational perspectives to help the company address emerging risks, resolve difficult questions, and make well-supported decisions.
Our work includes shaping and improving governance practices, supporting effective oversight, developing clear assessments and recommendations, and ensuring that decisions lead to action. We work closely with research, safety, security, legal, and product teams to identify gaps, reconcile different views, and improve our approach as capabilities and circumstances change.
About the Role
We are looking for a curious, high-agency Research Program Manager who can reason from first principles, make sense of incomplete or conflicting information, and move difficult work forward. You will help shape the substance of governance reviews, connect ideas and evidence across teams, and develop recommendations that are both well-founded and practical.
The work requires someone who can use established approaches where they fit, recognize when circumstances call for a different approach, and update their thinking as new evidence emerges. You should bring sound judgment, a willingness to experiment and learn, and the program-management discipline to turn good analysis into action.
Depending on your experience and the team’s needs, your work may focus on safety advisory and board-level oversight, deployment governance, or standards and strategic partner commitments.
In this role, you will:
• Bring together technical, policy, and operational inputs to develop coherent assessments, recommendations, and decision materials for governance bodies and senior leaders.

• Work through emerging or ambiguous questions, test assumptions, identify gaps or conflicting evidence, and help determine what additional analysis or decisions are needed.

• Engage critically with research, evaluations, safeguards, and risk assessments, working with the relevant experts to understand what the evidence supports and where uncertainty remains.

• Partner with governance-body chairs, technical leaders, and other stakeholders to shape substantive reviews, frame the questions that matter, and communicate conclusions clearly.

• Translate feedback, recommendations, and decisions into concrete work with accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, and clear criteria for completion.

• Drive that work forward across teams, resolve blockers, surface difficult tradeoffs, and escalate disagreements or resource gaps when needed.

• Help teams understand which governance processes apply, integrate reviews into research and deployment plans, and identify changes that require further consideration.

• Maintain clear records of decisions, rationale, conditions, commitments, exceptions, and unresolved questions.

• Help improve governance practices, standards, and guidance as capabilities, evidence, and circumstances evolve.

• Build and refine practical tools, operating cadences, and sources of truth that improve the quality and pace of the work.

• Develop trusted relationships across Research, Safety Systems, Preparedness, Security, Legal, Product, leadership, and relevant external partners.

You might thrive in this role if you:
• Have experience leading complex, cross-functional work in a research, technology, policy, safety, security, governance, or related environment.

• Take initiative, move quickly, and find practical ways forward when ownership, requirements, or the path to an answer are unclear.

• Are intellectually curious and can learn unfamiliar subjects well enough to ask sharp questions, test an argument, and recognize when deeper expertise is needed.

• Can synthesize complicated or conflicting information without losing important distinctions, limitations, or uncertainty.

• Write clearly and precisely, particularly when explaining difficult issues and recommendations to senior decision-makers.

• Bring strong program-management fundamentals and a record of turning ambiguous requests into work that gets finished.

• Exercise sound judgment in sensitive situations, navigate disagreement constructively, and know when to act independently or seek a decision.

• Are willing to try new approaches, learn from feedback, and change your mind when the evidence changes.

• Build useful structure without adding unnecessary process.

• Care deeply about the responsible development and deployment of increasingly capable AI systems.

Helpful experience:
• Research program management or strategy and operations in a technically complex organization.

• AI safety, preparedness, model evaluations, cybersecurity, or technical risk management.

• Advisory committees, board-facing work, executive decision support, or other consequential reviews.

• Translating policies, standards, or governance decisions into practical requirements and programs.

• Strategic partnerships or sensitive deployment contexts.

About OpenAI
OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.
For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement .

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. Staff, Third Party Risk Management

• Drive technical automation across the TPRM lifecycle by engineering custom AI agents, capabilities, and workflows to integrate tool outputs, optimize risk data processing and scale operations.

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

About the role

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to help build GitLab Duo Agent Platform, the agentic orchestration layer that runs AI agents and flows across the entire software lifecycle.

Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work.

The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on.

This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security.

What you'll do

• Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon.

• Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow.

• Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation.

• Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com.

• Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product

• Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each.

• Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product.

• Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration.

• Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. This reaches across:

• Design the extensibility surface so customers can build custom agents and flows, connect their own tools and internal systems, and bring external agents such as Claude Code and Codex into GitLab workflows without weakening the platform's guarantees.

• Drive down the cost and latency of agentic requests, and work with Product on how model selection, routing, and credit consumption behave as usage grows.

• Define the evaluation practice for the platform: offline benchmarks and online experiments that measure task completion, correctness, tool-call accuracy, latency, and cost per task, and that catch regressions before customers do.

• Build the governance and safety surface with Security and Compliance: policy-driven controls over which agents and models may run where, permission and identity semantics that align to existing roles and group structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, traceability of every flow session, and audit that stands up to enterprise review.

• Complete Interview Training and participate in hiring for the department as a technical interviewer or panel member.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years at Staff, Principal level or equivalent senior technical leadership.

• Hands-on production experience building on large language models: agent loops, tool calling, context management, retrieval, prompt and model evaluation. Experience shipping this to real users, not only prototyping it.

• Strong background in distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience under multi-tenant load.

• A track record of defining evaluation frameworks and using benchmark and experiment results to make architecture decisions, rather than shipping on intuition.

• Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls, safety guardrails, and responsible AI practices for systems that act on a customer's behalf.

• Ability to drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Security on problems that start out ambiguous.

• Experience mentoring senior engineers and shaping technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority.

• Comfort working in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, or TypeScript, and willingness to work across the stack the platform spans.

• Excellent written and asynchronous communication, and the ability to work effectively in a fully remote, globally distributed organization.

About the team

The AI engineering organisation is building the product and infrastructure that make GitLab an effective environment for running agents across the software development lifecycle. We’re distributed across the world and partner with teams throughout GitLab to help the GitLab Duo Agent Platform become the backbone of GitLab's AI features. You will report directly to the VP of Engineering for AI and especially work together with all the teams, the engineering management and other principal engineers in the AI department. This is an opportunity to lead a consequential group as AI changes how software is built.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . We're looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Repository Services team in GitLab's Create stage. Repository Services is a new team, and its first months are about reliability and support, so you'll spend real time on performance and structured query language tuning, caching, rate limiting, testing, observability, and resiliency, with experienced team members to lean on. You'll collaborate with product management, product design, testing, security, user experience research, technical writing, Gitaly, Code Review, and the other Source Code teams.

• Develop secure, well-tested, performant features and improvements using Ruby and GraphQL.

• Work through complex requirements and legacy constraints to deliver clear solutions while protecting the reliability of this critical system.

• Design and maintain backend services, application programming interfaces, data models, and business logic that control how code reaches a repository, who may change it, and how it is verified.

• Build on the primitives Gitaly provides and work closely with the Gitaly team.

• Triage and fix bugs and support requests for the features the team owns.

• Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, and involve domain experts when their input will improve the outcome.

• Use artificial intelligence agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output.

• Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews.

• Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency.

• Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

• Professional experience building backend web applications, services, or application programming interfaces, with experience using Ruby and GraphQL.

• An understanding of relational databases, structured query language, data modeling, caching, background processing, and backend performance practices.

• Experience contributing to user-facing workflows and maintaining their underlying systems.

• Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes.

• Experience using artificial intelligence coding agents and reviewing their output, or an interest in building these skills in a complex monorepo.

• Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including sharing useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.

Repository Services is a small backend team in the Create stage, formed in September 2026 when Source Code split into focused teams. We build on Gitaly's primitives and meet regularly with the Gitaly team, and our work serves GitLab.com , self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated.
